subject: Literature
title: Flannery O'Connor's Southern Gothic
description: A micro-lesson that makes Flannery O'Connor's Southern Gothic usable.

hook.text: Flannery O'Connor raised peacocks on a Georgia farm and wrote some of the most violent, funny stories in American literature.

buildup.text: Her stories feature grotesque characters, sudden violence, and moments of divine grace erupting through ordinary Southern life.

discovery.text: O'Connor said she wrote about the grotesque because 'for the hard of hearing you shout, and for the almost blind you draw large.'

twist.text: She wrote her greatest work while dying of lupus, producing masterpieces in the years she knew would be her last.

climax.text: O'Connor proved that a Catholic woman in rural Georgia could write stories that stand with the best in world literature.

punchline.text: She wrote with one eye on eternity and the other on peacocks.

quiz.question: Why did O'Connor write about grotesque characters and violence?
options: She believed Southern life was inherently violent
She said 'for the hard of hearing you shout, and for the almost blind you draw large'
